To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of waste plastic as an energy material is a viable solution to the waste plastic crisis.

waste plastic can be converted to energy in the form of heat, electricity and/or fuels; that the conversion of waste plastic to energy can be accomplished in a variety of ways, each of which has its own benefits and drawbacks; and that waste plastic can also be used as a feedstock for the production of a number of valuable chemicals.
the use of waste plastics as energy material can be a viable alternative to landfilling or incineration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of waste plastic in the design of novel polymer systems.
the design of polymers which are capable of being converted into energy in a controlled and efficient manner.
designing end-of-life plastics with a view to their conversion to energy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
waste plastic should be used as a valuable energy material.
waste plastic is an energy source, and that its conversion into a form that can be utilised for energy generation is the most sustainable approach to its management.

there is a dire need for a more efficient, cost effective and sustainable way to handle the waste plastic problem, which can be achieved by a more efficient design of end-of-life polymer products, which would be able to be recycled into high quality materials for use as energy materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to design end-of-life polymers with a focus on energy conversion, and that this is the only way to address the problem of plastic waste in a sustainable way.
the most efficient and sustainable approach is the use of waste plastics as a resource, rather than a waste product, by designing them for end-of-life as a source of energy.
we are developing a new class of materials, based on polymers, that are designed to be easily recycled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of waste plastic materials should focus on end-of-life energy recovery, rather than recycling, to achieve a more sustainable solution to the problem of waste plastic pollution.
end-of-life polymer design is an essential tool for the sustainable management of waste plastic.
the best solution for plastic waste will be a combination of several approaches, including recycling, incineration and chemical conversion.
